overview: The two ways an allele can behave in a heterozygote — one masks the other.
genZNote: Dominant shows up even with one copy. Recessive needs both parents to agree.

aspects.label: Expression in Heterozygote
aspects.valueA: Its phenotype is expressed even with just one copy (Aa shows the dominant trait).
aspects.valueB: Its phenotype is masked in the heterozygote; only shows up when homozygous (aa).

aspects.label: Notation
aspects.valueA: Represented by a capital letter, e.g. 'T' for tall.
aspects.valueB: Represented by a lowercase letter, e.g. 't' for dwarf.

aspects.label: Carrier Status
aspects.valueA: A dominant allele is never 'hidden' — if present, it is seen.
aspects.valueB: Can be silently carried by heterozygotes without showing the trait.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Dominant does not mean 'more common' or 'better' — it only describes masking behaviour in a heterozygote.
overlay.memoryTrick: Dominant = loud, shows up with one copy. Recessive = shy, needs both copies.
overlay.commonMisconception: A dominant allele is not necessarily the more frequent one in a population — frequency and dominance are unrelated.
